about: Held-out questions, written 2026-11-18 from site pages the main set doesn't cover. Never tune the bot against these: they're for an honest score. Same format as questions.json. ho-spenddown and ho-dsnp were moved to the main set on 2026-11-18 after the bot was fixed for them.

turns: How do I report someone who is getting Medicaid but shouldn't be?
questions.reference: Call the Investigations Office of the Benefits, Employment & Support Services Division at (808) 587-8444. Each health plan also has a fraud hotline.

turns: My health plan keeps ignoring my complaint. Who else can help me?
questions.reference: The Hawaii Medicaid Ombudsman helps members with problems with their QUEST Integration health plan, including grievances and appeals: toll-free 1-888-488-7988, O'ahu (808) 746-3324, TTY 711.

turns: My dad has been in a nursing home for months and wants to move back home. Is there a program that helps with that?
questions.reference: Going Home Plus helps Medicaid members who have lived in a hospital, nursing facility or ICF/ID for at least 60 days in a row move back into the community, including help finding housing and services. Open to all islands.

turns: How do I stop getting text messages from Med-QUEST?
questions.reference: Text STOP to 45421; you'll get a confirmation and no more messages. Text HELP to 45421 for help.
Early and Periodic Screening, Diagnostic and Treatment: preventive and comprehensive care (medical, mental and behavioral health, dental, treatment) for Medicaid members from birth up to age 21.

turns: How far ahead do I have to schedule a ride to my doctor?
questions.reference: At least 48 hours before the appointment, through your health plan; urgent visits within 24 hours can be booked with less notice.

turns: Do I have to pay for a Medicaid ride?
questions.reference: No: a covered Non-Emergency Medical Transportation ride costs nothing.

turns: What is the Hawaii Child Wellness Incentive Program and how do I apply?
questions.reference: A pilot paying parents on Medicaid $50 for each child's yearly well-child exam (children under 18). Steps: take the child for the exam, have the doctor complete section 2 of Form DHS 1193, then submit it through the program's web page or the MyDHS portal (mydhs.hawaii.gov), by email to HCWIP@dhs.hawaii.gov, by fax to 808-900-7978, or by mail. The card arrives in 4-6 weeks.

turns: Is there someone who can help me fill out my application?
questions.reference: Community partners can help with applications; you can also call 1-800-316-8005 or visit an eligibility office.
Yes: vision and hearing services are covered QUEST Integration benefits; check details with your health plan.

turns: I aged out of foster care and I'm 22 now. Can I still get Medicaid?
questions.reference: Yes, likely: Med-QUEST covers certain former foster care youth from 18 up to age 26. Apply to confirm.

turns: Where can I find the QUEST member handbook?
questions.reference: On the member resources / member handbook pages: the 2025 QUEST Member Handbook, plus each health plan's own handbook.

turns: I have a really bad toothache. Is emergency dental covered for adults?
questions.reference: Yes: for adults 21 and older, emergency and palliative dental treatment is covered. Call CCMC to find a dentist (O'ahu 808-792-1070, neighbor islands 1-888-792-1070).

turns: Eh how I renew my Med-QUEST? I wen get one pink letter
questions.reference: Renew online at medical.mybenefits.hawaii.gov, with the form that came with the pink letter, or by phone at 1-800-316-8005.

turns: Which health plans can I pick from?
Which one of those has the fraud hotline 1-855-973-1852?
Does Med-QUEST pay for drug or alcohol rehab?
questions.reference: Yes: medically necessary alcohol and chemical dependency services and substance abuse treatment are covered behavioral health services.

turns: I'm moving to California next month. What happens to my Med-QUEST?
questions.reference: Report the move (change of address) to Med-QUEST; Med-QUEST covers Hawai'i residents, so apply for Medicaid in the new state.
